title: Peters introduces bipartisan bill to require transparency about federal government's use of AI
source_used: The Alpena News (carrying a statement from Sen. Gary Peters)
key_facts: Sen. Gary Peters (D-Mich.), ranking member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, introduced the Transparent Automated Governance (TAG) Act.
Agencies would have to notify people when they interact with certain AI or automated systems.
Agencies would have to notify people when a critical decision about them is made using AI-augmented processes.
The Office of Management and Budget would issue guidance, including redress processes with human review of adverse AI decisions.
The text calls the bill bipartisan but names no co-sponsor.
quote_evidence: The Transparent Automated Governance (TAG) Act would require federal agencies to notify individuals when they are interacting with or subject to critical decisions made using certain AI or other automated systems.
The bill also directs agencies to establish a redress process ensuring there is a human review of critical decisions made using AI systems that may negatively affect individuals.
why_it_matters_hint: Would give people a right to know when government AI affects them and to ask for human review.
notes: The article reproduces a press statement from Peters's office; introduction date is not stated.
